verdicts.tldr: one view-less hook registered first lets a 17-view collection past Register's 16-kind cap, drops a published kind from the register event, and hides the badge elision mark
verdicts.details: publishedKinds takes token.ExtensionKindsUpTo(limit) in registration order, then drops kinds whose ExtensionView is nil, so a view-less hook inside the window spends one slot of the bound. Register calls publishedKinds(token, maxEventKinds+1) and only aborts when the filtered set exceeds 16; with 1 hook + 17 views the window keeps 16, the abort never fires and the event lists 16 of the 17 kinds GetExtensionKinds reports. extensionBadges does the same with maxBadges+1, so 1 hook + 10 views renders 8 badges and no ellipsis. Indexers reading the register event and readers of the page lose kinds with nothing marking the list partial. The realm is new in this diff (absent at the merge base). Fix: filter view-less kinds while walking and stop once limit published kinds are collected, bounding the walk separately if a hard cap on iterations is wanted.

verdicts.tldr: GetExtensionKinds costs quadratic gas in the issuer's own extension count; only that issuer's key is affected
verdicts.details: publishedKinds(v, 0) walks every kind and calls ExtensionView per kind, which re-scans led.extensions via lookupExtension, so the read is n(n+1)/2. Measured read cost 28.0M gas at 200 hooks and 107.3M at 400 (x3.83). The issuer pays the same quadratic shape to register them (setup 33.6M -> 118.4M), and the cost lands only on calls for that issuer's own key; no caller in the tree loops GetExtensionKinds over the registry, so it is a latent risk rather than a defect a maintainer would block. Fix: have ExtensionKindsUpTo return (kind, view) pairs, or add a single-pass helper, so publishedKinds is linear.

verdicts.tldr: an enumerable attached after minting is now published through the registry and reports TotalSupply 0 against a core supply of 2
verdicts.details: NewEnumerable now passes its view to coreLedger.RegisterExtension(led, view), so grc721reg.GetExtension hands it to any realm; attached after two mints it reports TotalSupply 0, TokenByIndex(0) errors, and after a transfer indexes only the moved token. The missing guard predates the diff (base NewEnumerable has the same body and the same 'Attach it before the first mint' comment); the diff makes the stale view reachable by third parties. It breaks a documented precondition, and consumers already trust issuer-supplied views wholesale, since any issuer can register a view of kind 'enumerable' returning anything. TestRegisteredCollectionStaysLive attaches royalty before any mint, not a late enumerable, so it does not present this case as supported. Fix: panic in NewEnumerable when core.TotalSupply() > 0.

Base enumerable/token.gno: 'coreLedger.RegisterExtension(led)' with the view returned only to the caller; grc721reg absent at base.

verdicts.tldr: the collection page shows 8 of 9 published kinds with no elision mark, and past the window the badge subset follows registration order despite the godoc
verdicts.details: extensionBadges calls publishedKinds(v, maxBadges+1) and marks elision only when i == maxBadges; a view-less hook in the 9-slot window leaves 8 published kinds, so the page shows 8 badges and no ellipsis while GetExtensionKinds returns 9. Separately, sorting happens after the window, so 10 views registered kind9..kind0 render kind1..kind8 plus the ellipsis and never kind0, contradicting the publishedKinds godoc that sorting makes output independent of registration order. Readers of Render lose published kinds with no sign the list is cut; it shares its root cause and fix with candidate 1. Fix: filter view-less kinds before applying the limit, and either sort over the full set or drop the order-independence claim from the godoc.
